reading.body:
Google does not publish megawatt capacity at the individual building level for its Council Bluffs campus in Iowa. The facility is part of a larger regional footprint where Google has invested over $20 billion since 2007, including a $7 billion expansion announced for Council Bluffs and a new Cedar Rapids site, backed by a NextEra Energy agreement to restart the Duane Arnold nuclear plant. Without disclosed power figures, the campus cannot be ranked by consumption, but it sits among 52 mapped facilities in Iowa, of which only 2 operators publish capacity figures at all.

The absence of published capacity makes this campus invisible to any analysis of whether it matters to AI scaling by power. Google's state-level disclosure policy deliberately withholds the megawatt figures and square footage that would let a reader assess whether Council Bluffs is a training cluster, inference farm, or storage facility, or how much of Iowa's power budget it commands. The $20 billion investment suggests material scale, but scale in Iowa means little without knowing whether the power comes from the grid, nuclear, or renewable contracts, and whether it is already constrained.

Any reader deciding whether this campus matters must work backward from Google's regional power agreements and capital commitments rather than from disclosed specifications. The Duane Arnold nuclear restart is the only published vector connecting this facility to grid constraint or AI capability density, and Google has not disclosed what fraction of Council Bluffs load it will serve or whether it is sufficient for planned expansion.
